change: Same-image configuration experiment: node-wide archive byte budget 256 versus 512 MiB; production defaults and durability proofs unchanged.

control.label: control
control.method: Same frozen executable, control 256 MiB then candidate 512 MiB node-wide archive byte budget. Only the archive byte budget changes. Production default unchanged; same quorum/log/image proof, bounded queues and no timed mutation retries. Cold benchmark VM restart and fresh persistent internal node volumes for each cohort; RustFS on original external VM disk. Three pinned 1-vCPU / 3-GiB nodes, each with 500 leaders and 1000 followers; 1500 three-voter groups. Four SQL workers with 16 reservations each, four archive-cut slots, 500-ms ticks, 24 writers, two 180-second windows. Exact 4500 replica values and 1500 RustFS archive positions verified separately. Shared-host activity and boundary cgroup CPU counters retained. All data and images preserved. This sequential pair is not randomized or isolated.

method_limits: One sequential control-first comparison on a shared host; reversed-order confirmation remains required.
Both cohorts use the exact same image and load AST, three pinned 1-vCPU/3-GiB nodes, 1500 three-voter groups and fresh persistent volumes.
Only configured archive byte budget changes; container memory, entry cap, producer/worker counts, tick interval, load and durability remain fixed.
Timings overlap and have different operation counts; they are not additive latency components. No sorted sample/receipt positional joins.
Boundary archive progress and final catch-up do not establish continuous backlog bounds or a RustFS saturation rate.
No timed mutation retries. Error-free verified cohorts are required; reconciliation cannot turn a failed window into a pass.
